sources.reviewed_note: Rebased our stack onto upstream tag v0.10.0 (2026-09-11, 'Initial build for Deep North'), which is the tip of master - there are no commits after the tag. Read the delta as a whole rather than commit by commit: 2774 upstream commits since our old base 50d333d. One of our seven was dropped by the rebase as already upstream ('Remove unused using that breaks builds outside Visual Studio'), and one new one was needed: v0.10.0 targets release-day 1.0.0 and references UpscaledFrameBuffer.UpdateCurrentRenderScale and m_targetResolutionVertical, neither of which exists in 1.0.12, so the frame-scaling patch was removed. sources.local_changes: Branch neuralyze/v0.10.0: seven commits on upstream v0.10.0. Six carried over from neuralyze/local (non-VR HarmonyPrepare guards, csproj SkipReleasePackaging condition, the BodyPose workaround, startup-stage reporting, name-based tracker role resolution, and the Mono/Linux plus no-base-assetbundle build fixes) and one new: 'Drop the frame-scaling patch Valheim 1.0 removed the target of'. sources.published_note: GPL-3.0 source offer. Branch neuralyze/local pushed to the fork 2026-08-25 at 23f0ce4526cd and publicly reachable; the portal links it from the world page and from the release pages of releases carrying a flat_companion or vr_runtime (PORTAL_VHVR_SOURCE_URL). Correspondence is anchored per binary, not per release version, because release versions are the portal's and mean nothing upstream: each published ValheimVRMod.dll gets a tag shipped/valheimvrmod-<first 12 hex of its sha256> on the commit it was built from. Pushed so far: shipped/valheimvrmod-f879224e030c -> 23f0ce4526cd, the DLL inside vr-runtime-2.2.5-nospawnprobe.zip served as hrafnheim-vr 2.5.111 and doggerland/storgard/vangard-vr 2.5.36. mcs is not reproducible - two compiles of one tree differ in ~77800 of 600064 bytes - so a build is matched by size plus source markers, not by hash.
sources.correspondence_gap: Audited 2026-08-26 by hashing ValheimVRMod.dll inside all 1793 published zips under the artifact root. Seven distinct binaries are published and exactly one carries a shipped/ tag, so the previous claim that every published build is tagged was wrong about six of them; the offer text on the pages has been corrected to say what is true per binary. Two of the seven can never be given a tag: 3fe2ce08 (the Flat companion, 147 releases) and c2519916 (an earlier Flat companion, 2 releases). Each holds part of commit 1d6ea02 without the rest of it - both carry the two "Non-VR companion mode" literals that enter the history only at 1d6ea02, 3fe2ce08 lacks the HarmonyPrepare typeref added by 5ea5183 (an ancestor of 1d6ea02) and c2519916 has it, but neither has 1d6ea02's own LogDiagnostic - and no commit can hold a descendant's strings without its ancestor's, nor half of a single commit. The cause is that the seven commits were authored on 2026-08-18 by grouping finished changes into themed commits rather than replaying how the tree evolved: the non-VR branch was written by 07-26 and HarmonyPrepare and LogDiagnostic by 07-28, but they were committed in the opposite order, so builds taken from the tree in between fall between the commits. Correcting an earlier note: the reflog does not start 2026-08-18, it starts 2026-07-26 04:15:44 with the clone of upstream at a10f24fc - 43 minutes before 3fe2ce08 was compiled - and it still does not help, because the intermediate tree was never committed. Searched and not found: no commit, no stash, no dangling object (the four dangling blobs are the vhvr-0.9.21*.zip archives), and no second copy of the source - a find for ValheimVRMod.cs across every mounted big drive returns exactly one checkout. Closing those two therefore needs a rebuild from a commit on the branch and a republish, which is a deliberate publish decision and not a repo change; until then the offer names both binaries and says we cannot name their revision, which is the honest state rather than a discharged-looking one.

sources.why: The container the world operation scripts drive. valheim_provision.py reads its default.env for the PGID a world's mounts are chowned to.
sources.reviewed_note: Read all 18 commits and the 14 files they touch. Material to us: Debian 12 then 13 base-image upgrades with 32-bit glibc restored, busybox cron replacing Debian vixie-cron, a UMASK calculation change that would land on the world directories provisioning chowns, and secrets support. The libdoorstop env-var rename (DOORSTOP_ENABLED/DOORSTOP_TARGET_ASSEMBLY) is already in our tree: our local commit 3ad0632 made the same fix independently, so upgrading converges and that part of our patch can be dropped. Upgrade deferred to a maintenance window because it replaces the base image under four live worlds; filed as a bead.
sources.local_changes: Four local commits, none of them upstream, published to https://github.com/neuralyze/valheim-server-docker branch neuralyze/local (we have no push access to community-valheim-tools, so that fork is the only off-host copy): 40252fce 'Update local Valheim server runtime', 3f736897 'Apply directory permissions to Valheim 1.0 world directories', 43844851 'Sync BepInEx patchers so preloader patches survive a rebuild', and f000f97f 'Never sync the download cache over the install when the update failed'. The last one is load-bearing: valheim-updater's download-failure branch logged "an existing version was found locally - using it" and then fell through to 'rsync -a --delete dl/ server/', which overwrote a correct 1.0.12 install with a stale 0.221.12 cache and reported it as "already the latest version". That silently downgraded three worlds on 2026-09-13 and emptied their saves - see bead vhp-oxn. Note also that docker-compose.yaml carries uncommitted operator changes (CONFIG_DIR/DATA_DIR made required rather than defaulting to a shared directory, WEBMAP_PORT dropped); those are deliberate and predate this session.

sources.why: Server-side character storage, and the mechanism this fleet uses to hand out tiered kits and skills. TEMPORARY SITUATION, changed 2026-09-14 and again 2026-09-15: we compile this mod ourselves and install that build on the Ulfsland server and on the clients of its four editions, and since 2026-09-15 our build is PATCHED - upstream's template code equips nothing and hardcodes item quality to 1, which made the entire jumpstart kit system deliver unarmoured characters holding unupgraded gear. Nothing of the mod is committed to this repository and nothing of it is published outside the operator's own machines; our patches ARE committed, because they are our own text and they are what keeps the divergence honest. Listed here because it is third-party code that reaches players through us, and because both the licence position and the reason this is temporary have to be written down rather than rediscovered.
sources.source_index: our own build of upstream source; see build_note. The Hexium route (index_api below) is still implemented in tools/valheim_mods.py and cmd/profile-definition-builder but is no longer used for this package.
sources.pinned_version_note: OUR version string, not an upstream release. Upstream's ModVersion at bb7d3cd6 is 1.4.17; the fourth component marks the local patches in tools/servercharacters/patches/. Upstream only ever publishes three components, so this can never collide with a real release, and System.Version - which ServerSync.VersionCheck.IsVersionOk parses these strings with - orders 1.4.17.1 above 1.4.17.
sources.artifact_sha256_note: OUR build of bb7d3cd6 PLUS tools/servercharacters/patches/: ServerCharacters.dll as compiled by tools/servercharacters/build.sh, declaring ModVersion 1.4.17.1. The UNPATCHED build of the same commit is efe7d42149bf721bbfaa4dc0e5cd3d8f1d4c95c992ebf111c1b7029fadedde26 and was reproduced byte-for-byte on 2026-09-15 before the patches were written, which is how we know the divergence is the patches and nothing else. For reference, the author's own 1.4.17 DLL is 0b497b7e830365bc57d0a5ada200e9e571b0f3e3625ac08de06a2bc528850872 inside archive 7f17f1164579bf58c8fce1408e2b2471e64ef98961fd91f382a208f4d04b187f on Hexium; we do not ship those bytes and never did.
sources.archive_sha256_note: The Thunderstore-shaped archive built around that DLL with a manifest.json of our own, 486149 bytes, byte-reproducible. This is the SHA256 the four ulfsland-* profile definitions must carry for Smoothbrain-ServerCharacters, and the digest cmd/valheim-profile-sync checks the copy embedded in itself against. It REPLACES 6cdb18180d279757729df8a28d326a3b31e13165d6bf73a7c1001bc9f72a6f82 (482416 bytes, the unpatched build); republishing the four definitions and the four clients together is not optional, because a client carrying either archive is refused by a server running the other.
sources.reviewed_note: Thunderstore's newest is 1.4.16 (2025-05-02) and it MUST NEVER be installed on Valheim 1.0.12: PlayerProfile.GetCharacterFolderPath moved to SaveSystem, so ServerCharacters.Initialize throws MissingMethodException at FejdStartup.Awake and the mod never initialises - while the Harmony patches on PlayerProfile.LoadPlayerFromDisk, Player.Load, Skills.Load and Inventory.Load are already installed, leaving live save/load patches over an uninitialised profile store. Seven further members are unresolvable against 1.0.12's assembly_valheim; all eight are fixed by upstream commit bb7d3cd6 ('fix for deep north', 2026-09-09), which is 1.4.17. Verified by resolving every type and member reference in the shipped binary against the running server's assemblies: 486/488 typerefs and 5159/5178 memberrefs resolve, and the unresolved remainder is byte-for-byte the same set as in an independent from-source build of bb7d3cd6 - System.Numerics.Vector intrinsics plus one ImmutableArray span overload, both supplied by Unity's BCL at runtime. Details in tools/servercharacters/README.md.
sources.local_changes: SOURCE CHANGES: one patch, tools/servercharacters/patches/0001-template-quality-and-equip.patch, applied by build.sh to the bb7d3cd6 checkout. Read the patch for the delta; the behavioural divergences it produces are, one line each: (1) CharacterTemplate.yml gains a `quality` map, prefab -> quality, and granted items are added at that quality instead of the literal 1 upstream hardcodes - MEASURED in upstream's IL as `ldc.i4.1` in the third AddItem argument, which made every `quality: 3` in every preset a lie; (2) the quality is clamped at runtime to [1, m_shared.m_maxQuality] read live from ObjectDB and the clamp is logged, because Inventory.AddItem never clamps it (MEASURED: it stfld's m_quality straight from the argument and reads m_maxQuality nowhere), and an over-max item silently becomes non-upgradeable; (3) CharacterTemplate.yml gains an ordered `equip` list and those items are equipped through Humanoid.EquipItem(item, triggerEquipEffects: false), where upstream equipped nothing at all - the string EquipItem occurs ZERO times in upstream's whole assembly, so every templated character spawned unarmoured and unarmed holding a full kit, and a granted BeltStrength was a 2 kg no-op because SE_Stats.m_addMaxCarryWeight only reaches SEMan through SetupEquipment -> UpdateEquipmentStatusEffects, which walks the equipped slot fields only; (4) the list is walked BACKWARDS, because EquipItem unequips whatever holds the target slot, so the last successful equip for a slot wins and walking backwards makes the FIRST name in the list win - which is the order a preset author writes when a kit carries two chest pieces; (5) equips the game refuses are retried from a Player.Update postfix once `IsSwimming() && !IsOnGround()` clears, that being the only guard in EquipItem that can be transiently true at spawn; (6) CharacterTemplate.yml gains a `contents` map, container prefab -> (prefab -> count), which fills a Vapok-AdventureBackpacks backpack through ABAPI.GetBackpack(itemData).Value.Inventory reached ENTIRELY by reflection - AdventureBackpacks has no version handshake (MEASURED: zero hits for ServerSync / ModRequired / MinimumRequiredVersion in its assembly) and ServerCharacters must still load where it is absent, so a compile-time reference would be a plugin that fails to load; (7) the three deserialiser sites share one builder with IgnoreUnmatchedProperties, so an unknown top-level key is ignored and logged instead of throwing; (8) the catch clauses widen from `catch (SerializationException)` - a type YamlDotNet never throws, so upstream's handler never fired - to also catch YamlException, and the template-apply one logs instead of swallowing; (9) ModVersion and MinimumRequiredVersion move from 1.4.17 to 1.4.17.1. Nothing else: no retargeting, no publicizing beyond the publicized GAME assemblies upstream's own build expects. Three support files under tools/servercharacters exist only because upstream's build cannot run on this host and are not part of the mod: ServerCharacters.csproj (upstream's wants a NuGet packages/ tree and hand-publicized assemblies), publicize.cs, and Request.cs, which upstream generates from Request.proto with protogen - a .NET tool this build cannot run - and whose members were read back out of the shipped assembly with Cecil and reproduced exactly.
sources.build_note: tools/servercharacters/build.sh clones bb7d3cd6 into a temp directory, applies every patch in tools/servercharacters/patches/ with `git apply` (no --3way: the commit is pinned, so a patch that fails to apply is something a human must look at), refuses to continue if the patched source still declares upstream's own ModVersion, compiles it in a throwaway dotnet/sdk:8.0 container, ILRepacks it, and writes internal/servercharacters/embedded/ServerCharacters.zip. That path is GITIGNORED: the archive is built or placed locally and never committed, because this repository is published and committing an unlicensed third-party binary is the difference between the operator's private choice about their own machines and public redistribution. The PATCHES are committed, and are text we wrote - they are the provenance record and they are what makes the divergence reviewable. internal/servercharacters embeds whatever is at the archive path; the client and the definition builder both read it from there, so the bytes a client writes and the SHA256 a definition publishes cannot disagree.
sources.authorisation: The operator instructed the from-source build on 2026-09-14, for their own server and their own player group, knowing the licence position: 'go ahead and use servercharacters 1.4.17 for now because it will get updated on thunderstore soon and we will fix the legal issue in the next couple days', and, when asked which delivery route, 'i didnt say use the hexium path.. i mean the compile from source'. They authorised MODIFYING it on 2026-09-15 - 'go ahead and modify the mod all you want' - and asked for the backpack work in the same session: 'also, see if you can add equipped and filled backpacks to default servercharacter as well'. It applies to Ulfsland only - the four ulfsland-* profiles - and to no shared profile, so no Hrafnheim, Doggerland, Storgard or Vangard client receives it.
sources.redistribution: The licence facts are unchanged, and modifying the mod does NOT change them - it only makes them matter more. The repository has no LICENSE file, so it is all rights reserved, and on 2026-09-11 the author refused a public request (issue #98, 'Fork and LICENSE') to fork and redistribute a MODIFIED build - 'No, sorry. Especially not on Thunderstore.' Since 2026-09-15 a modified build is exactly what we run, which is the precise thing he declined, so the boundary that keeps this inside the operator's own choice is the ONLY thing separating the two: we publish no copy anywhere public, commit no copy, and host no copy on the portal's own pages; the bytes travel only from this host to the operator's own clients, inside the client executable they download from the operator's own portal. The patches under tools/servercharacters/patches/ are OUR text and are committed; the mod's own source is not, and the binary is not. Do NOT commit the binary, publish it to Thunderstore or any index, offer it on a public page, or ship it to any world outside Ulfsland. If the situation outlives the operator's 'next couple of days', it needs the author's permission or removal.
sources.operational_risk: Version skew WITHIN a release is gone by construction: the server plugin and every client's embedded copy come from one archive, so ServerSync's MinimumRequiredVersion 1.4.17.1 / ModRequired true cannot be unsatisfiable. What replaces it is a build dependency - a publish from a tree whose archive is missing fails naming tools/servercharacters/build.sh, and a client built from a tree with a DIFFERENT archive refuses the install with a message telling the player to download the current client rather than joining with a mismatched assembly. ACROSS the 1.4.17 -> 1.4.17.1 step there are two hazards, and the second is the dangerous one. First, VersionCheck.IsVersionOk is SYMMETRIC (ours >= their minimum AND theirs >= our minimum), so a 1.4.17 client is refused by a 1.4.17.1 server AND a 1.4.17.1 client is refused by a 1.4.17 server: there is no mixed-fleet window, and a player who has not re-synced simply cannot join. That failure is loud and harmless. Second, the TEMPLATE must not move ahead of the DLL. A 1.4.17 DLL throws YamlDotNet.Core.YamlException on the `quality` / `equip` / `contents` keys - MEASURED by deserialising a new-schema template against upstream's real PlayerTemplate type, which has exactly {skills, items, spawn} - and upstream's `catch (SerializationException)` does not catch YamlException, so the exception escapes the Game.SpawnPlayer postfix and the ENTIRE template is discarded: no skills, no items, no custom spawn, a naked character at the world default spawn. CharacterTemplate.yml is hot-reloaded by a FileSystemWatcher and ServerSynced as text with no restart, so dropping a new-schema template onto a server still running the old DLL ruins every character created in that window. ORDER: new DLL to the server and to all four client editions FIRST, every player re-synced, and only THEN the new-schema template. 1.4.17.1 itself ignores unknown top-level keys and logs them, so this hazard exists once, for this step, and not again.
sources.retire_when:
The author publishes 1.4.17 or later to Thunderstore, or we stop using the mod. NOTE that retiring is no longer a pure subtraction: the Thunderstore build will not carry the `quality`, `equip` or `contents` keys, so swapping to it silently returns every templated character to unarmoured-and-unarmed with quality-1 gear. Retiring therefore means EITHER getting these three keys upstream (tools/servercharacters/UPSTREAM-request-1.4.17-release.md is the existing channel) or accepting that the jumpstart presets lose equipping and quality, which means re-authoring tools/jumpstart/presets and the CharacterTemplate.yml generator too. Once that is settled: `valheim_mods.py --profile

add Smoothbrain-ServerCharacters` replaces the whole arrangement, and every block marked 'TEMPORARY: local ServerCharacters build' comes out - internal/servercharacters and its embedded/ directory, the local-build branches in cmd/profile-definition-builder and cmd/valheim-profile-sync (including cmd/valheim-profile-sync/servercharacters_package.go and its test), LOCAL_BUILD_PACKAGES and local_build_package in tools/valheim_mods.py, the .gitignore entry, and tools/servercharacters/patches/. The Hexium backend stays: it is the mechanism for the next mod that lives off Thunderstore.
sources.checkout_note: Not a checkout of the upstream repository - we keep none. build.sh clones bb7d3cd6 on demand into a temp directory, applies tools/servercharacters/patches/ to it, and deletes it. The artifacts retained are the gitignored archive under internal/servercharacters/embedded/ and the committed patches, which are ours.
